notSupersededBy.ND:marijuana-specific-summary-pardon-or-: N.D.C.C. ch. 12-55.1 executive summary pardon. A different body, a different instrument and a different relief. The memo's own self-help stop conditions name a participant confusing the two as a stop condition.
notSupersededBy.ND:general-conviction-sealing-under-n-d-: The memo records that the § 19-03.1-23(9) seal is STRONGER than Chapter 12-60.1 sealing, because once sealed the record may not be opened even by order of the court. A stronger, mandatory-on-the-elements relief is not absorbed by the weaker discretionary one.

supersessionCheckedFirst.whatThisCheckDoesNotClaim: It establishes that the route is current in this repository and unheld. It does not re-verify N.D.C.C. § 19-03.1-23(9) against the current official host; the Nationwide source inventory is absent from this worktree, so no acquisition was performed and none is claimed.

vehicleDetermination.instrument: Motion to Seal Court Record Under N.D.C.C. § 19-03.1-23(9)
vehicleDetermination.filedIn: the existing criminal case that entered the judgment of guilt
vehicleDetermination.court: the court that entered the judgment — District Court or Municipal Court, which the packet cannot hard-code
vehicleDetermination.destination: Clerk of Court of that court
vehicleDetermination.confirms: The memo's nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal outputStrategy of custom_pleading, and closes the ND vehicle map's 'Not determined here' for this route.
vehicleDetermination.ruleApplied: Form vs Custom Pleading: an official form is used where one controls. The publishing body states it has no forms for criminal matters, so a Grade-A composed pleading is appropriate and is not a substitute for a form that was merely not found.

sourceThisRestsOn.title: Sealing DUI Records (N.D.C.C. Section 39-08-01.6) — A Research Guide for a North Dakota State Court Process
sourceThisRestsOn.publisher: North Dakota Legal Self Help Center
sourceThisRestsOn.quote: The ND Legal Self Help Center can't provide assistance with court process in criminal cases and doesn't have forms, procedures, or expertise available in this area.
sourceThisRestsOn.andAlso: If you represent yourself, you need to conduct your own legal research, determine the appropriate procedures, and create your own legal documents.
sourceThisRestsOn.whyItReachesThisRoute: The statement is about court process in CRIMINAL CASES as a class, not about the DUI statute. A § 19-03.1-23(9) motion is filed in the participant's existing criminal case, so the same statement covers it. This is the guide's own scope, not an extension of it to a neighbouring subject.

vehicleDetermination.whatThisDoesNotClaim: It does not establish that no prescribed form exists anywhere in North Dakota for this motion. A district or municipal court could maintain a local form. The determination is that the current statewide self-help guidance prescribes no form and directs the filer to draft one, which is sufficient to choose a composed pleading and is not sufficient to assert a statewide negative. If a local form is later found, that form controls for that court and this determination yields to it.
vehicleDetermination.correctsNothingInTheMemo: The memo already said custom_pleading with outputStrategyStatus resolved. What was missing was a source for it; the memo's own component note asserted that 'the official research guide confirms no sealing forms are published' while citing the Chapter 12-60.1 guide, which is a guide to a different statute. That inference is replaced here by a quoted statement about criminal matters generally.

theTwoYearCondition.statutoryText: the court shall seal the court record of that conviction if the person is not subsequently convicted within two years of a further violation of this chapter
theTwoYearCondition.theAmbiguity: The two-year period has no anchor on the face of the subsection. The memo records the question as counsel_confirmation_required and classifies it impact release_blocker.
theTwoYearCondition.notResolvedHere: This record does not pick an anchor. Quoting a statute faithfully is not the same as reading it correctly, which is the lesson of the reverted Oregon bindings, and the memo's own classification is counsel_confirmation_required. The counsel question stands exactly as the memo states it: does the two-year period run from the judgment of guilt or from the further violation?
theTwoYearCondition.whatWasMeasuredInstead: Whether the unresolved anchor has leaked into a participant-facing answer.

measurement.corroboration: The factory-v2 census row for this route carries separateGates.paymentAllowedAtTheEvaluator false, which agrees.
measurement.finding: The engine does not guess the anchor. It detects that the waiting rule was not executed, terminates at needs_review and refuses payment. The unresolved blocker has produced a refusal rather than a wrong answer, which is the correct behaviour and is the same discipline the 12-60.1 determination requires: where more than one reading qualifies, do not silently invent a preferred one.

theTwoYearCondition.consequenceForTheBlockerClassification: The blocker is real and remains open, but its current cost is that the route does not sell, not that a participant is told the wrong thing. It is a counsel blocker, not a live participant-facing defect.

theHazardThisRecordExistsToName.why: The refusal above is the only thing standing between this route and a legally wrong waiting period sourced from another statute. Anyone repairing nd.waiting_rule_not_executed must know that.
theHazardThisRecordExistsToName.mechanism: src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts, bestWaitingRuleForPathway, builds its candidate pool from the profile-wide waitingPeriodRules PLUS the pathway's own waitingRules, mapping each prose string through parseDurationFromText, then scores candidates by token overlap with the pathway id, label and summary.
theHazardThisRecordExistsToName.measuredPool: All thirteen of this pathway's compiled waitingRules parse to a duration. Only three of them carry the § 19-03.1-23(9) two-year period. The other ten carry durations from four different North Dakota authorities.

foreignDurationsInThisRoutesOwnPool.belongsTo: N.D.C.C. ch. 12-55.1 marijuana summary pardon (Pardon Advisory Board), no convictions in the past five years
N.D.C.C. ch. 12-60.1 misdemeanor conviction sealing, no new conviction for at least 3 years before filing
N.D.C.C. ch. 12-60.1 felony conviction sealing, no new conviction for at least 5 years before filing
N.D.C.C. § 39-08-01.6 DUI record sealing, no later DUI or any other criminal offense within seven years
N.D.C.C. ch. 12-60.1 hearing timing, not a waiting period at all
N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-05 nonconviction closing, the court's own deadline, not a waiting period at all

exclusionRulesAreContaminatedTheSameWay.note: None of the three is an exclusion under § 19-03.1-23(9).
entries: The ch. 12-55.1 summary pardon eligibility description, which belongs to a different route.
The ch. 12-60.1 45-day hearing rule, which is a timing rule and not an exclusion.

The § 39-08-01.6(2) commercial-driver exclusion, which is the DUI statute's exclusion. A commercial driver is not excluded from sealing a first marijuana possession conviction, and this string asserted as an exclusion on this route would be wrong.

theHazardThisRecordExistsToName.whatMustNotHappen: Repairing nd.waiting_rule_not_executed by letting a duration be selected out of that pool. Three years, five years, seven years, forty-five days and ten days are each wrong for this subsection, and each would look plausible in a result page. The repair is to scope the pathway's rule set to its own statute and to execute the statute's own two-year condition once counsel has answered the anchor question — in that order.
theHazardThisRecordExistsToName.ownership: The compiled profile and the evaluator are engineering-lane surfaces. This record determines the legal content and names the hazard; it changes neither, and it authorizes no route.
